'''''Oxalis latifolia''''' is a species of flowering plant in the [[Oxalidaceae|woodsorrel family]] known by the common names '''garden pink-sorrel'''<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=17 October 2014 }}</ref> and '''broadleaf woodsorrel'''.<ref>{{PLANTS|id=OXLA6|taxon=Oxalis latifolia|accessdate=30 January 2016}}</ref> It is native to [[Mexico]] and parts of Central and South America. However, it has propagated to other parts of the world.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dulal |first=Dipesh |date=18 October 2024 |title=My kids love Oxalis latifolia Kunth (Chari amili/amilo) |url=https://www.dipeshdulal.com.np/2024/10/chari-amilo-oxalis-latifolia-kunth.html |access-date=19 October 2024 |website=Dipesh Dulal |language=en-EN}}</ref>

==Description==
[[File:Oxalis latifolia.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Leaf detail]]
This is a perennial herb growing from a system of small [[bulb]]s and spreading via [[stolon]]s. There is no stem. The leaves arise on long [[Petiole (botany)|petioles]] from ground level, each made up of three widely heart-shaped leaflets about 4.5 centimeters wide. 

The [[inflorescence]] is an array of several flowers, each with five pink petals (some varieties have white flowers).

===Invasive species===
It is known on most other continents as an [[introduced species]] and a [[noxious weed]] and [[invasive species]], as it infests many types of agricultural crops. 

In south-eastern Australia, it is found in gardens, on roadsides, disturbed sites and is most likely a garden escape.<ref>[https://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&lvl=sp&name=Oxalis~latifolia Oxalis latifolia Kunth] by PlantNET (The NSW Plant Information Network System). Royal Botanic Gardens and Domain Trust, Sydney.</ref> It is spread by conveyance of soils containing the plant’s [[bulbil]]s, as well as by [[Surface runoff|runoff]]s, ants, and by larger animals like dogs and birds.<ref>[https://weedsofmelbourne.org/fishtail-woodsorrel-oxalis-latifolia Fishtail Woodsorrel (Oxalis latifolia)] by Weeds of Melbourne</ref>
